contexts.text: Still they are in charity; and therefore to hearken is predicated of them. ().
Abram hearkened to the voice of Sarai () = that it could not be done otherwise.
Their ear is uncircumcised, and they cannot hearken (). The ear uncircumcised = no hearkening, and that the Word was a reproach to them.
Under Ear, see this reference. AC 4653. AC 9397. AE 808.

Because thou hast hearkened to my voice () = through the union of the Lord's Human Essence with His Divine Essence... To hearken to the voice = that He underwent the last of temptation, and thus united the Human Essence to the Divine Essence. AC 3381.

To hearken to my voice, when predicated of the Lord, = to unite the Divine Essence to the Human one through temptations; for it is from these that in the Word obedience is predicated of the Lord. AC 3381:2, Explained.
Only hearken unto my voice... () = from the effect. To hearken to the voice = to obey. AC 3611.
Under Hear, see this reference. AC 3869. AC 5017. AR 87. AR 356. AE 14. AE 108. AE 249. DWis 10:4.
Ye hearkened not () = non-reception. To hear, or to hearken, = to obey; and as it = to obey, it also = to receive; for he who obeys what faith dictates, the same receives.
If thou wilt hearken to His precepts () = obedience, and a life according to the goods of faith. To hearken = obedience and life.
Moses hearkened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did all that he said () = the effect according to the ordination of the Divine good.
To hear and do, thus to hearken.
To hearken a hearkening () = life according to that doctrine.
To hearken () = to obey and to be instructed.
He that hath an ear let him hear = he who understands and hearkens to what the Lord teaches in the Word.
By Simon is meant hearkening and obedience.

Hearkening, which is obedience, corresponds to the hearing of the ears; and therefore both the hearing and the ears are correspondences; and the action of obedience into the hearing, in order that a man may prick up his ears and attend, is influx. Hence it is that to hearken, and to hear are both significative; to hearken, and to hear to anyone = to obey; and to hearken and hear anyone = to hear with the ears.
